title: Mexican Monarchists
capsule: The Mexican Monarchists represented the Conservative faction that invited Archduke Maximilian of Austria to accept the Mexican crown, backed by a French expeditionary force dispatched by Napoleon III following the Liberal government's 1861 suspension of foreign debt payments. Maximilian accepted the crown in April 1864 after a stage-managed 'popular' petition and was formally installed as Emperor of Mexico on 10 April 1864. His reign was contested from the outset by Benito Juárez's republican forces; after US pressure forced Napoleon III to withdraw French troops in 1866–67, Maximilian refused to abdicate, was captured by republican forces at Querétaro, and executed on 19 June 1867.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The monarchist government's effective territorial control fluctuated dramatically through the civil conflict; the polygon likely overstates coherent governance and reflects nominal rather than operational sovereignty.
